question: Given observational samples and an assumed known causal DAG, can a query-agnostic structural causal model for mixed continuous and categorical tabular variables make each learned parent-to-child mechanism directly inspectable and symbolically simplifiable, while retaining competitive observational, interventional, and—where identifiable—counterfactual accuracy?

key_findings.claim: KaCGM makes a deliberately falsifiable additive-noise approximation rather than identifying the true SCM from observational data.
key_findings.evidence: Each continuous node is modeled as x_j = KAN_j(pa(j)) + u_j. The proposed checks are HSIC between each inferred residual and its parents, dHSIC across residuals, and observational MMD/C2ST relative to a more flexible model. The authors explicitly state that passing these checks only means misspecification was not rejected; it cannot confirm that the true SCM or its mechanisms were recovered.

key_findings.claim: For categorical nodes, a Logistic-KAN can reproduce the learned conditional law and its downstream interventional distribution without identifying a point-valued discrete exogenous noise.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition IV.1 represents a categorical conditional through inverse-CDF sampling with u_j ~ Uniform(0,1). Its appendix proof shows that intervening on a parent substitutes that value into the learned conditional and that convergence of the conditional weights induces convergence of descendant distributions. This is distributional interventional equivalence, not recovery of the original discrete structural assignment.

anchors.section: Appendix A / Proof of Proposition IV.1

key_findings.claim: The mixed-data model does not support arbitrary unit-level counterfactuals: a point-valued answer is claimed only when every descendant of the intervention is continuous and each continuous noise-to-observation map is injective.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition IV.2 excludes interventions having any discrete descendant. The appendix proof relies on abducting a unique residual for continuous descendants and then propagating it in topological order; categorical descendants break this uniqueness, for which the paper points to counterfactual bounds instead.

anchors.section: Appendix A / Proof of Proposition IV.2

key_findings.claim: The observational diagnostics respond in the intended direction when additivity is progressively violated, whereas a more flexible causal flow remains well fit.
key_findings.evidence: Across ten realizations of a 6,000-sample three-node SCM, alpha continuously changes the last mechanism from additive at alpha=0 to nonadditive. Figure 2 shows KaCGM's observational/interventional matching, counterfactual error, HSIC, and dHSIC worsening as alpha grows, while CFlow continues to approximate the distributions and residual independence. This is a positive sensitivity demonstration, not a calibrated acceptance threshold or guarantee.

key_findings.claim: On the eleven continuous additive benchmark SCMs, classical ANM is numerically best; the two KAN variants are merely not rejected as worse in the authors' aggregate post-hoc comparison.
key_findings.evidence: With 1,000 training and 1,000 validation samples per graph, ANM has observational MMD 8.86±2.6×10^-3, interventional MMD 3.02±2.5×10^-3, and counterfactual MAE 2.62±2.5×10^-2. KAN records 16.49±8.1×10^-3, 4.79±4.1×10^-3, and 5.10±2.4×10^-2; KAAM records 16.76±9.6×10^-3, 4.76±5.1×10^-3, and 4.66±2.3×10^-2. Their post-hoc p-values against the best are 0.061 and 0.055, so the evidence is non-rejection, not equivalence or superiority.

key_findings.claim: Explicit categorical likelihoods improve the mixed-data benchmark relative to rounding continuous generators, but they do not dominate every individual metric.
key_findings.evidence: Across the eleven SCMs after x3 is made ternary, KANmix and KAAMmix both obtain RF interventional accuracy 0.52±0.01 and post-hoc p=0.690. KAAMmix has interventional MMD 6.29±4.33×10^-3, versus ANM's 6.22±5.16×10^-3; ANM also has the best observational MMD, 1.22±0.44×10^-3, while KAAMmix has 1.60±0.78×10^-3. The result supports modeling the categorical conditional directly, but the table's claim that the mixed models are 'best across all metrics' is stronger than the displayed per-metric numbers.

key_findings.claim: The semi-synthetic Sachs experiment cleanly exposes KaCGM's negative scope: it is competitive only when the generated mechanisms satisfy the additive restriction.
key_findings.evidence: With 1,000 training and 1,000 validation samples, additive Sachs gives KAN observational/interventional MMD 1.36±0.41 and 1.95±0.67 (both ×10^-3) and counterfactual MAE 3.50±1.40×10^-2, compared with ANM's 1.12±0.28, 1.30±0.21, and 1.28±0.43. In the nonadditive version, KAN degrades to RF observational accuracy 0.67±0.13, observational MMD 5.27±9.20×10^-3, and counterfactual MAE 3.42±1.54×10^-2; CFlow is best overall at 0.55±0.03, 1.42±0.35×10^-3, and 1.84±0.99×10^-2.

key_findings.claim: The real cardiovascular example demonstrates audit artifacts, not validated real-world causal effects.
key_findings.evidence: Assuming the supplied DAG is correct, the authors report that KaCGMmix has the best observational RF accuracy and MMD among their compared models, but less favorable independence diagnostics. Pruning preserves observational fit and symbolic substitution slightly worsens it. No interventional or counterfactual ground truth exists for this dataset, so the case study cannot establish correctness of the reported treatment effects.

key_findings.claim: After pruning and symbolic substitution, the ischemia mechanism becomes a compact polynomial logit from which the paper reads off intervention effects.
key_findings.evidence: The displayed logit contains quadratic and linear terms for standardized age, BMI, and systolic pressure, plus 0.743·diabetes and intercept -1.871. The PDP-derived average treatment effects are approximately -0.42 logit units for reducing BMI from 35 to 20 and -0.59 for reducing systolic pressure from 180 to 120. These numbers are model-implied under the assumed DAG and learned equation, not clinically identified effects with uncertainty intervals.

key_findings.claim: Interpretability is conditional on revalidating every simplification and refitting the residual distribution; symbolic replacement is not a free post-processing step.
key_findings.evidence: The pipeline selects the shallowest statistically competitive KAN, prunes weak edges, symbolically substitutes atomic functions, and reruns observational and independence checks at each step. The authors warn against a simplification when checks worsen and state that the residual distribution must be re-estimated after each modification, otherwise distribution matching deteriorates.

key_findings.claim: KaCGM's auditability carries substantial fitting cost compared with classical ANM and, on Sachs, causal flows.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix Table III reports KAN training times of 374.90±53.51 s on additive Sachs and 385.17±66.42 s on nonadditive Sachs; KAAM takes 356.39±20.92 s and 345.11±49.96 s. ANM takes 0.28±0.25 s and 0.20±0.21 s, while CFlow takes 1.49±0.51 s and 9.33±9.12 s; only DBCM is slower at roughly 483–502 s.

key_findings.claim: The broad framing of jointly achieving expressive causal generation and transparency should be read as an additive-regime trade-off, not as a general expressivity result.
key_findings.evidence: The conclusion acknowledges approximation bias for strongly nonadditive, entangled, or heteroscedastic mechanisms, shows CFlow/DBCM outperforming in the nonadditive Sachs regime, and states that diagnostic success cannot guarantee true structural recovery. Thus the paper's strongest defensible claim is competitive adequacy when low-complexity additive mechanisms fit, with unusually inspectable functions.

method.core_idea: Represent every continuous structural assignment in a known DAG as an additive-noise KAN and every categorical conditional as a Logistic-KAN, then accept, prune, and symbolically simplify the resulting simulator only while observational distribution and inferred-noise independence diagnostics remain satisfactory.
method.mechanism: Nodes are trained in causal order. For a continuous child, a KAN or zero-hidden-layer KAAM regresses the child on its parents; residuals are treated as samples of its exogenous noise and their empirical distribution is fitted. For a categorical child, a sigmoid/softmax KAN learns p(x_j|pa(j)), with an implicit Uniform(0,1) inverse-CDF structural realization. Observational samples draw root/noise variables and propagate through the graph; interventions replace selected assignments; continuous counterfactuals abduct residuals and reuse them after the intervention. Model selection minimizes a random-forest two-sample accuracy on child-plus-covariate observational samples. The interpretability pass favors shallow KANs, prunes low-importance edges, fits formulas from polynomial/trigonometric/exponential atoms, refits residual laws, and exposes per-parent probability-radar and partial-dependence plots.
assumptions: The causal DAG and its topological order are known and correctly specified; the paper does not perform causal discovery.
Causal sufficiency holds, so node-wise exogenous variables are jointly independent and there are no hidden confounders.
Continuous mechanisms are adequately described by homoscedastic additive noise, x_j = g_j(pa(j)) + u_j; passing residual tests cannot prove this assumption.
Observations are i.i.d. from one stable data-generating process, and empirical residual distributions support the interventions being queried.
A learned categorical conditional is sufficient for downstream interventional distributions, while point-valued categorical counterfactuals are generally not identified.
Point counterfactuals for continuous descendants require an injective map from each exogenous variable to its child given its parents.
A low-complexity spline decomposition exists if symbolic auditability is desired; deeper KANs may fit but are progressively harder to inspect.
MMD, random-forest C2ST, HSIC, and dHSIC have enough power at the available sample size to expose practically important misspecification.
Any pruning or symbolic substitution is followed by residual-law refitting and repeated adequacy checks rather than treated as semantics-preserving by construction.

techniques.role: Uses learned univariate edge functions and sums/compositions to parameterize each parent-to-child structural mechanism.
Infers a continuous node's exogenous realization by subtracting the learned parent function and reuses it for unit-level counterfactual propagation.
Models binary or categorical node conditionals with sigmoid/softmax KANs while leaving the discrete exogenous variable implicit.
Applies HSIC node-wise and dHSIC jointly to look for residual dependence that contradicts causal sufficiency plus additive specification.
Uses Gaussian-kernel MMD and random-forest C2ST, including comparison with more flexible generators, to screen density mismatch from observational data alone.
Removes weak KAN edges and approximates remaining univariate functions with closed-form atoms, subject to repeated fit checks.
Turns explicit structural logits into individual probability-radar decompositions, population partial-dependence curves, and model-implied ATEs.
Selects each node model from KAN, diffusion, or flow grids using observational child-and-covariate C2ST performance.

evaluations.result: KaCGM's distribution errors and dependence diagnostics worsen as alpha introduces nonadditive noise
evaluations.baseline: CFlow retains good distribution matching and inferred-noise independence under the nonadditive mechanism; the true SCM supplies the oracle reference

limitations: Author-stated: strongly nonadditive, highly entangled, or heteroscedastic structural equations create approximation bias; CFlow and DBCM outperform KaCGM in the paper's nonadditive regime.
Author-stated: pruning and symbolic substitution trade fidelity for transparency; the cardiovascular symbolic stage measurably worsens observational diagnostics.
Author-stated: passing observational distribution and residual-independence checks cannot guarantee recovery of the true structural equations.
Author-stated: causal sufficiency and a correctly specified causal graph are assumed; hidden confounding or graph errors invalidate the generative and counterfactual interpretation.
Author-stated: symbolic equations and visual diagnostics become difficult as the graph and mechanism complexity increase, limiting the approach to moderate-dimensional tabular settings.
Author-stated: mixed-data point counterfactuals are unavailable whenever an intervention has a categorical descendant; only distributions or bounds remain identifiable.
Reviewer-identified: the eleven core synthetic DGPs are themselves additive-noise models, structurally favoring ANM/KaCGM, and the mixed version discretizes only one ternary node.

Reviewer-identified: the real cardiovascular case assumes its graph, lacks interventional ground truth, and reports model-implied ATEs without uncertainty; it demonstrates auditability rather than clinical causal validity.

Reviewer-identified: treating p>0.05 against the best method as evidence that KaCGM is 'not worse' does not establish statistical equivalence, and the phrase 'best across all metrics' conflicts with Table I's per-metric ANM values.

Reviewer-identified: Appendix C says hyperparameters are selected child-by-child using observational RF/C2ST accuracy, which is also a reported outcome; the paper does not document a nested holdout distinct from the validation set, and tuning budget, selection reuse, and selection uncertainty are not incorporated into the error bars.

Reviewer-identified: the method's runtime is hundreds to thousands of times ANM on Sachs and much slower than CFlow there, so the accuracy–interpretability trade-off also includes a material computational cost.

Reviewer-identified: the study does not test graph misspecification, hidden confounding, missing data, covariate shift, high-cardinality categorical variables, or extrapolative interventions outside observed support.
failure_modes: A wrong DAG or latent confounder can make node-wise residuals dependent and invalidate intervention propagation; weak HSIC/dHSIC power may nevertheless fail to flag it.
Nonadditive or heteroscedastic noise cannot be absorbed into an independent additive residual, biasing both abducted counterfactuals and generated interventions.
A discrete descendant makes the unit's latent category draw non-unique, so deterministic abduction-action-prediction produces an unjustified point counterfactual.

Pruning a small-looking edge can remove a causally important effect in a narrow region; symbolic substitution can then magnify the error under intervention even when global observational metrics barely change.
Polynomial symbolic approximations can extrapolate sharply outside the observed standardized covariate range, making apparently transparent ATEs unreliable for distant interventions.
At small sample sizes, flexible KAN edge splines can be poorly estimated and two-sample/independence tests can lack power, so both fitting and the proposed acceptance gate degrade together.
A categorical conditional learned by softmax can match observed class frequencies yet misrepresent counterfactual coupling across worlds, which the observational likelihood cannot identify.
Selecting the shallowest model that is not significantly worse can choose an underfit mechanism when the comparison test is underpowered.
If residual distributions are not refitted after pruning or symbolic replacement, observational and interventional samples inherit a mismatched noise law by construction.
reusable_insights: For an interpretable causal simulator, validation should target both the observed joint law and the defining independence structure of its inferred exogenous variables.
Failure to reject misspecification is an operational deployment gate, not evidence that a structural model has been identified.
Mixed-variable SCMs require separating distributional intervention validity from point-counterfactual identifiability; the latter is strictly stronger.
Symbolic distillation of a structural mechanism should be treated as a new model: refit its noise law and repeat all adequacy checks after every simplification.
A transparent model can be useful even when a black-box baseline predicts better, but the comparison should expose accuracy, query scope, and runtime jointly.
When the graph is known, node-local interpretable functions make it possible to audit direct causal paths without conflating them with ancestor shortcuts in a monolithic generator.
Negative-regime experiments are especially informative for structured models: deliberately violating additivity reveals whether the diagnostics and performance fail together.
open_questions: Can a KAN-based conditional normalizing flow preserve useful symbolic structure while handling nonadditive and heteroscedastic exogenous transformations?
How should HSIC, dHSIC, MMD, and C2ST thresholds be calibrated into a preregistered accept/reject rule with finite-sample error control?
Can partial well-specification certify a restricted set of intervention targets even when other mechanisms or parts of the graph fail diagnostics?
How robust are the extracted formulas and ATEs to graph uncertainty, latent confounding, missingness, and interventions outside observed support?
Can discrete counterfactual uncertainty be reported as sharp bounds or distributions while retaining the same auditable KAN conditional mechanisms?
Does symbolic simplification remain stable on substantially larger mixed-type DAGs with high-cardinality categories and interactions?
What is the accuracy–auditability Pareto frontier under matched hyperparameter-search time and wall-clock budgets against TRAM-DAG, causal flows, and diffusion SCMs?
Can dependence-minimization be included in training, rather than used only as a post-hoc diagnostic, without hiding misspecification through optimization?

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretable Neural Causal Models with TRAM-DAGs
competitive_landscape.difference: TRAM-DAG already targets an interpretable, flexible SCM with a known DAG, mixed continuous/ordinal/binary variables, and queries across Pearl's three levels; it therefore narrows any broad 'first interpretable neural causal model' claim. KaCGM instead uses additive KAN edge functions, residual-independence falsification, pruning, and explicit symbolic formulas/plots; TRAM-DAG uses transformation models and also analyzes selected continuous counterfactual structures with unobserved confounding.

competitive_landscape.title: CausalKANs: interpretable treatment effect estimation with Kolmogorov-Arnold networks
competitive_landscape.difference: CausalKANs already combines KAN estimators with pruning, symbolic simplification, closed-form formulas, and interpretable plots, but only for conditional treatment-effect estimators. KaCGM extends the toolkit to a full query-agnostic SCM with one mechanism per DAG node, exogenous-noise diagnostics, mixed categorical conditionals, intervention sampling, and restricted counterfactual abduction.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal normalizing flows: from theory to practice
competitive_landscape.difference: Causal normalizing flows learn invertible, path-preserving SCM maps from a known graph or ordering and answer observational, interventional, and counterfactual queries, including mixed-data and partial-graph experiments. Their invertible flows cover nonadditive mechanisms and are less directly symbolic; KaCGM trades that density flexibility for inspectable additive KAN equations and explicit residual-independence diagnostics.

competitive_landscape.title: Modeling Causal Mechanisms with Diffusion Models for Interventional and Counterfactual Queries
competitive_landscape.difference: The diffusion-based causal model assigns a deterministic diffusion encoder-decoder to each node, obtains a latent proxy for exogenous noise, and handles all three query levels under causal sufficiency. It is a more flexible but opaque and computationally heavy mechanism class; KaCGM uses additive spline functions whose residuals and symbolic form can be audited, and openly fails in the nonadditive regime where diffusion is competitive.

competitive_landscape.title: VACA: Designing Variational Graph Autoencoders for Causal Queries
competitive_landscape.difference: VACA uses a variational graph autoencoder with architectural graph constraints to approximate observational, interventional, and counterfactual distributions without parametric structural equations, assuming a known graph and no hidden confounders. KaCGM models nodes separately with additive KANs and categorical likelihoods, enabling residual tests and closed-form mechanism extraction but accepting a stronger functional restriction.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Structural Causal Models for Tractable Counterfactual Inference
competitive_landscape.difference: Deep SCMs compose normalizing-flow and variational mechanisms to abduct exogenous noise and answer all three causal levels, including high-dimensional image and medical examples plus discrete mechanisms. KaCGM is specialized to moderate-dimensional tabular DAGs and contributes inspectable KAN equations plus observational misspecification checks rather than high-dimensional generative capacity.

competitive_landscape.title: DeCaFlow: A deconfounding causal generative model
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct prior removing a central scope assumption
competitive_landscape.difference: DeCaFlow is a query-agnostic causal generator trained once from observational data and a graph, but it targets continuous systems with hidden confounding and proves correctness for queries identifiable by do-calculus or sufficiently informative proxies. KaCGM instead assumes causal sufficiency and contributes inspectable additive KAN mechanisms, mixed categorical conditionals, and symbolic extraction; DeCaFlow therefore narrows any implication that hidden confounding is an unavoidable limitation of current causal generators rather than a deliberate price of KaCGM's auditability.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first KAN-based causal generative model for mixed tabular data, together with an observational validation pipeline and an automated pruning/symbolic framework that preserves query-agnostic observational, interventional, and counterfactual semantics.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper supplies a node-wise KAN/Logistic-KAN SCM, two mixed-query propositions and appendix proofs, HSIC/dHSIC plus MMD/C2ST checks, symbolic edge pruning, eleven-DAG and Sachs experiments, and a real formula-extraction case study. Primary records show that causal flows, diffusion SCMs, VACA, Deep SCM, and DeCaFlow already provide query-agnostic deep causal generation across broader functional or confounding regimes; TRAM-DAG already provides interpretable mixed-type neural SCMs; and CausalKANs already combines KANs with pruning and symbolic treatment-effect formulas.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the particular integration of KAN structural assignments, additive-residual falsification, mixed categorical conditionals, and formula extraction inside a full SCM. It is not the first interpretable neural SCM, the first mixed-type query-capable causal generator, the first query-agnostic generator robust to confounding, or the first use of KANs and symbolic pruning in causal estimation. The novelty is meaningful but combinatorial and its empirical advantage is interpretability under adequate additivity, not superior causal accuracy or general expressivity.

reviewer_notes: Independent secondary review read every page of the pinned 14-page arXiv:2603.20184v1 artifact, including the complete main text, references, both proposition proofs, Algorithms 1–5, the full hyperparameter grids, all eleven benchmark SCM equations, the mixed-variable construction, and Table III runtimes. The indexed PDF SHA-256 348fd35aba2522231ce9d499b2542830509ecc6e3ffab9cadb62b674520ae5e5, text SHA-256 e878ceaef7897e506f36337d34768d39663ae204946a17ea20ef4715091c95a7, page count 14, and extraction timestamp match fulltext_index.jsonl exactly; the official record still identifies v1 as current on 2026-08-23. Every finding, evaluation, number, and page anchor was rechecked. Negative/contradiction audit: ANM is numerically best on the continuous additive table; p>0.05 is non-rejection rather than equivalence; the mixed KAN variants do not own every best Table I cell despite the prose claim; nonadditive Sachs favors flexible flows; the cardiovascular ATEs have neither causal ground truth nor uncertainty; and Appendix C tunes on observational RF/C2ST without documenting a separate nested test set. Figure-only cardiovascular diagnostics remain qualitative. Author-stated limitations are kept distinct from reviewer-identified evaluation and deployment boundaries.
